description: The hand-verified expected result for the DERIVED Trivy feature fixture, oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/derived-trivy-features.json. Every value was derived by reading that fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/, never by running the adapter and recording what it printed. This file is the companion of expected/trivy.rows.json, which covers the captured positive fixture: the capture is byte-identical to harness/artifacts/raw/trivy.json and therefore holds only the three DS-0026 misconfigurations that artifact holds, so the vulnerability and secret sections, the package-coordinate precedence, the multi-valued CweIDs array and the per-record path refinement are exercised here instead. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/trivy.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match.
scanner_class: per record -- vuln, secret or misconfig -- taken from the section array the record was read from. Trivy is the one tool in AAP 0.5.4's class table whose scanner_class is not fixed, and this file is where that variation is pinned.
scanner_class_derivation: The enclosing section array decides the class and nothing else does. adapters/trivy.py fixes the mapping once in SUPPORTED_SECTIONS, resolves it through scanner_class_for_section(section), and hands the section name to adapt_record as a required argument; no branch of that function consults a record's own fields, and a section outside those three yields an unattributable_section rejection rather than a class. Every scanner_class below is therefore checkable by re-walking the fixture and reading which array the record sits in.

scanner_class_falsifiability.why_the_content_misleads: Every piece of prose on this record points at the secret scanner. Its Title is "Secrets passed via `build-args` or envs or copied secret files", its Message is "Possible exposure of secret env \"SPARK_HOME\" in ENV", its Resolution talks about secret mounts, and its Namespace is builtin.dockerfile.DS031. Any implementation that keyed the class off record content -- a search for the word secret, a guess from the rule identifier, a try-all-three read of VulnerabilityID then RuleID then ID -- would class this row secret.
scanner_class_falsifiability.why_misconfig_is_correct: It is an element of Results[0].Misconfigurations[], and the section array is the sole source of the class. SUPPORTED_SECTIONS maps Misconfigurations to misconfig, so this row is misconfig. The record's words are a finding about a Dockerfile that mentions secrets; they are not a statement about which scanner produced it.
scanner_class_falsifiability.what_this_row_falsifies: This single row is what makes the section-not-content derivation falsifiable. An implementation that read record content would emit secret here and still satisfy every other assertion in this file, because no other record's prose disagrees with its array. If this row ever reads secret, the derivation has been inverted. That is the failure this fixture exists to catch and it is not a value to update.
scanner_class_falsifiability.corollary: The same rule runs the other way on row 2, whose RuleID is jwt-token: it is a secret because it sits in Secrets[], not because its identifier names a token format.

derived_from.kind: authored to the shape Trivy declares, not copied from an artifact. Stated as an object rather than as one sentence so each half of the provenance -- where the shape came from and where the records came from -- is separately checkable.
derived_from.shape_source: harness/artifacts/raw/trivy.json for the report envelope and the Results[] element shape, and Trivy 0.74.0's pkg/types/report.go for every member name this adapter reads. That is why the members are spelled as Trivy spells them and why no member appears that Trivy does not emit.
derived_from.record_source: authored. None of the nine finding records below appears in harness/artifacts/raw/trivy.json, in any file under harness/artifacts/logs/, or in oss-scan-results/findings.json. They were written to exercise adapter behaviours the pinned tree gave Trivy no opportunity to produce.
derived_from.history: this document was this module's positive fixture, under the name fixtures/trivy.json, until that name was taken by the byte-for-byte capture of harness/artifacts/raw/trivy.json. It was moved here verbatim rather than deleted, so the ten feature cases enumerated below stayed covered while the primary positive fixture became a true capture (AAP 0.6.2).
derived_from.byte_identical_to_its_predecessor: yes. The bytes under this name are the bytes that were under fixtures/trivy.json before the split, sha256 baa20547c89c73bcffaacb33924da2a6ea9782db4c1b0840a50b6cb6cc648313 either way, so every row and every counter this file states was already asserted against exactly these bytes and none of them was re-derived to fit a changed document.
derived_from.not_a_capture: no part of this document may be read as evidence of what Trivy reported. CapturedFixtureProvenanceTest asserts that this file is declared derived, that it is not the raw artifact and that it does not share the artifact's digest, so the claim is enforced rather than merely written.

fixture.provenance: DERIVED, NOT CAPTURED, and stated as such in the one place a reader looks. This file's fixture is not an excerpt of harness/artifacts/raw/trivy.json and is not byte-identical to it: the raw artifact is 3,496 bytes holding 3 records and this fixture is 12,226 bytes holding 9, its ReportID and CreatedAt are not the artifact's, and none of the nine records below appears in harness/artifacts/raw/ or in any file under harness/artifacts/logs/. The AAP 0.6.2 requirement that a primary positive fixture be an unmodified captured excerpt is satisfied by oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/trivy.json, which is a byte-for-byte copy of the raw artifact (sha256 979ad0ffbec3502f62ea0e2cd46fae549aaa5e1b7cc4a0d59153a5c2448766ec, 3,496 bytes) and is asserted against it record by record by CapturedFixtureProvenanceTest. This fixture exists alongside it, not instead of it.

why_this_derived_fixture_exists.summary: The captured artifact reaches three of this adapter's behaviours and no more, because the twelve authoritative globs contain no dependency manifest for the vulnerability scanner to resolve and no matched secret for the secret scanner to report. Deleting the cases below rather than moving them here would have shrunk coverage to what one clean Dockerfile scan happens to contain.
feature_cases_only_this_fixture_carries: the Vulnerabilities section, and with it scanner_class 'vuln' -- 5 records over four elements
the Secrets section, and with it scanner_class 'secret' -- 2 records, one carrying a fully redacted Match
the section-to-class variation across all three sections at once, including the falsifying misconfiguration at /Results/0/Misconfigurations/0 whose every piece of prose names secrets
three of the four package-coordinate precedence levels: the record's own PkgIdentifier.PURL, an enclosing Packages[] entry's Identifier.PURL, and a composed <ecosystem>:<name>@<version>
a multi-valued CweIDs array, ['CWE-1333', 'CWE-400'], whose producer order disagrees with the ascending-numeric rule
a per-record path refinement through PkgPath, on a Target ('Node.js') that names an ecosystem rather than a file
records carrying CVSS score tables while a mapped label governs, which is what makes label-over-score falsifiable
four kept rows whose paths lie outside the twelve globs, so in_scope false is exercised on real lockfile paths
a Results[] element holding an empty finding array, so results_without_supported_section is non-zero
Licenses and ExperimentalModifiedFindings present and empty on every element, which is the 'validated empty' passing case the captured artifact cannot show because it carries neither key at all
why_this_derived_fixture_exists.what_it_is_not: It is not evidence about what Trivy reported over the pinned tree. Every count in oss-scan-results/tool-status.md and every trivy row in oss-scan-results/findings.json comes from harness/artifacts/raw/trivy.json alone, and this fixture contributes to neither. It is an adapter input, and nothing else.

fixture.shape_fidelity: A Trivy 0.74.0 filesystem report carrying all three supported finding sections. Every member this adapter reads appears in report.go's own spelling: Results[] with Target, Class and Type; the three finding arrays; Packages with Identifier.PURL; MisconfSummary; CauseMetadata.StartLine; PkgIdentifier.PURL; PkgPath; CweIDs; and a CVSS table keyed by source.
fixture.fixture_is_never_edited_to_suit_these_ro: These rows are re-derived when the fixture changes, which is what the recorded sha256 above makes visible. The fixture is the input and this file is the assertion; the dependency runs one way.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent. emit.OPTIONAL_FIELDS is the authority and holds exactly the five named above.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each in-scope row matched, and the reason each out-of-scope row did not, are recorded per row under row_derivations.

resolution_context.root_independence: Every Target in this fixture is already root-relative and the recorded path base for trivy is the scan root itself, so joining onto the base and relativizing back to the root returns the reported string unchanged. The one per-record refinement is likewise root-relative. These rows therefore hold for whatever absolute scan root the adapter is given, and no absolute path appears anywhere in this file.
resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the trivy entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.why_the_merged_artifact_is_root_relative: The runner invokes trivy fs once per scope directory, because that subcommand takes exactly one path, and its merge step prefixes every part's Target with that part's own ArtifactName and sets the merged ArtifactName to ".". The metadata records that, which is why the base is the scan root rather than any one directory.
resolution_context.path_base_caveat: That base holds for the merged artifact only. The same metadata records that the eighteen retained per-directory reports under logs/trivy.parts/ are not root-anchored and must be read with per_section_target semantics and an explicit section_base. This fixture is the merged shape, so section_base is null and passing one would be wrong rather than harmless.
resolution_context.target_is_the_base: path comes from the enclosing Results[].Target, refined by a per-record path where the section supplies one. Only Vulnerabilities declares such a field -- PkgPath -- so a secret and a misconfiguration take their Target unrefined. paths.resolve_trivy_path owns every base decision; the adapter relativizes, joins and strips nothing itself.
resolution_context.per_record_refinement_in_this_fixture: Exactly one, on row 8. Its Target is "Node.js", which names an ecosystem rather than a file, and its PkgPath names the manifest the package was found in. The refinement is relative, is not the Target restated, and "Node.js" is not a container -- paths.ARCHIVE_EXTENSIONS holds .jar .war .ear .zip .tar .tgz .tar.gz .aar .nupkg .whl .egg and not .js -- so it resolves against the recorded base and the row's path is the manifest. No archive-member serialization arises anywhere in this fixture.
resolution_context.path_kind: tree_file on all nine rows: no path carries an ! and none begins with a .. segment, so non_filesystem_paths is 0 and no row is excluded from scope on kind alone.
resolution_context.severity_source: Every one of the nine records states a Severity label that is in severity.py's mapped vocabulary, so the label governs on all nine and no CVSS score is consulted on any of them -- AAP 0.5.4's precedence, visible here as severity_basis label on every row while four records do carry a CVSS table. severity_native keeps the literal exactly as the artifact wrote it, in upper case, and severity_norm is the band that literal maps to.
resolution_context.severity_mapping_exercised: CRITICAL to Critical, HIGH to High, MEDIUM to Medium, LOW to Low, and UNKNOWN to Info. The UNKNOWN row is the one worth reading twice: UNKNOWN is a mapped literal that bands to Info, not an unmapped literal, so its basis is label and severity_basis_unmapped_literal stays 0.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: Three of the four precedence levels appear. The record's own PkgIdentifier.PURL supplies three rows; a PURL on the matching enclosing Packages[] entry supplies one, which is the level a reader most easily skips; the ecosystem coordinate <lower-cased Results[].Type>:<PkgName>@<InstalledVersion> supplies one; and the field is absent on the four secret and misconfiguration rows, where absence is ordinary rather than a rejection.

counts.raw_count_unit: Results[] x one element of Vulnerabilities[], Secrets[] or Misconfigurations[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile._count_trivy walks independently of row construction, summing only the three supported sections
counts.row_order: Results[] in document order, the three sections in SUPPORTED_SECTIONS order within each element, and each section's elements in order. The rows below are in that order, and each row's index is its row_index under row_derivations.

unsupported_finding_sections.state_in_this_fixture: present and empty on every one of the six Results[] elements
unsupported_finding_sections.expectation: validate_finding_sections returns None. An unsupported finding section that is present and empty satisfies "validated empty" and does not halt, so this file is that passing case and records it explicitly rather than by the silence of not mentioning it.
unsupported_finding_sections.not_to_be_blurred_with: The non-empty twin is the halt fixture oss-scan-results/adapter-tests/fixtures/halt-trivy-unsupported-section.json, whose expected file records trivy.UnsupportedTrivySection. Nothing in this file expects a halt, and nothing in that one expects a row.

results_holding_no_record.reading: Its Vulnerabilities array is present and empty, so it contributes no record and therefore no row. That is a scanned target with nothing to report, counted under results_without_supported_section and never a rejection. Two of the three lockfile Targets in this fixture do carry records -- dev/package-lock.json with two and docs/Gemfile.lock with two, four kept rows with in_scope false -- and this third one carries none; the distinction is the fixture's, not a dropped row.

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/trivy.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): twenty-three authored keys, then one records_* per supported section, one rows_class_* per scanner_class, one path_kind_* per normalize.paths.PATH_KINDS member and one severity_basis_* per normalize.severity.BASIS_VALUES member. The order above is that order.
counters_note: Three of these are worth reading against the rows rather than taken on trust. known_non_finding_object_lists is 1 because Results[2] carries a two-entry Packages inventory -- an object array that is not a finding section, so it neither halts nor contributes a record, and it is the array that makes row 5's coordinate come from the enclosing-package level. results_without_supported_section is 1 for the empty-sectioned sixth element. severity_cvss_entries_present is 4 against severity_basis_cvss_score 0, which is the precedence made checkable: four records carried scores and none of the four was consulted, because each also carried a mapped label.

aap_reported_counters.note: The four counters AAP 0.5.4 has reported per tool. multi_location_records is 0 because no misconfiguration here carries a CauseMetadata.Occurrences array and a vulnerability and a secret each name exactly one location. multi_valued_cwe_records is 1: row 4's record lists CWE-1333 before CWE-400, so producer order disagrees with the ascending-numeric rule and the emitted value is CWE-400. multi_valued_cve_records is 0 because cve is collected from VulnerabilityID alone, which holds one identifier. non_filesystem_paths is 0 because every resolved path names a file in the scanned tree.

corroboration.why_unavailable: The dataset's three trivy rows are the three DS-0026 misconfigurations of the run's own artifact, and none of the nine records below is among them -- this fixture exercises sections and shapes the twelve in-scope globs gave Trivy no occasion to produce. So there is no after-the-fact agreement to record here. The captured fixture's expected file, expected/trivy.rows.json, does have that agreement and records it.
corroboration.consequence: Every value in this file rests on the fixture and the authored contracts alone, which is where AAP 0.6.1 puts it in any case: hand-verified from the fixture. The absence of corroboration is recorded rather than left for a reader to notice, because a value nothing else confirms should be labelled as such.

row_derivations.scanner_class_source: the enclosing section array is Misconfigurations, which SUPPORTED_SECTIONS maps to misconfig. See scanner_class_falsifiability above: this is the record whose content says secret.
row_derivations.rule_id_source: /Results/0/Misconfigurations/0/ID -- the field _SECTION_RULE_ID_FIELD names for this section
row_derivations.message_note: Title is preferred over Description, and Message is deliberately not consulted for a misconfiguration: this record's Message is "Possible exposure of secret env \"SPARK_HOME\" in ENV", which is the located instance rather than the finding's name, and _SECTION_MESSAGE_FIELDS names only Title and Description for this section.
row_derivations.start_line_note: A misconfiguration states its line inside CauseMetadata; _SECTION_START_LINE_PATHS tries the top-level StartLine first, finds none, then reads CauseMetadata.StartLine. 62 is within the file's real length.
row_derivations.cwe_absent_reason: CweIDs is declared on DetectedVulnerability only, so a misconfiguration carries none by the artifact's shape
row_derivations.cve_absent_reason: cve is collected from VulnerabilityID, which this section's records do not carry
row_derivations.package_coordinate_absence_is_not_a_reje: Misconfigurations is outside _DEPENDENCY_ORIENTED_SECTIONS: this is a finding about a file, not about a package, so the field is legitimately absent and the record still becomes a row.
row_derivations.in_scope_note: The glob's mid-path ** matches the docker/ segment, which is what makes this Dockerfile in scope at all; the path carries no src/test.
row_derivations.file_anchors_at_the_pin: line 20 is FROM ${java_image_name}:${java_image_tag}, line 62 is ENV SPARK_HOME=/opt/spark -- exactly the ENV this record names -- and line 71, the last, is USER ${spark_uid}

row_derivations.scanner_class_source: the enclosing section array is Misconfigurations
row_derivations.message_note: Again Title rather than Message. The Message here quotes the whole apt-get command line; the Title is the finding's name.
row_derivations.start_line_note: 36, with the record's EndLine at 48. The row takes the start line only; 36 is within the file's real length.
row_derivations.package_coordinate_absence_is_not_a_reje: same as row 0: the section is not dependency-oriented
row_derivations.file_anchors_at_the_pin: line 36 is RUN set -ex && \ and line 48 is the rm -rf of the apt lists, which is the block this record's Message quotes

row_derivations.scanner_class_source: the enclosing section array is Secrets, which SUPPORTED_SECTIONS maps to secret -- not the RuleID jwt-token, which is content
row_derivations.message_note: For a secret, _SECTION_MESSAGE_FIELDS puts the already-redacted Match first, which is AAP 0.5.4's clause for this section. This record's Match is fifty-two characters, every one of them an asterisk: Trivy redacted the value before writing the artifact, so the message carries the redaction and no character of any secret. Title and Description sit behind Match only so that a secret record lacking one is not rejected -- which is row 3.
row_derivations.no_secret_value_reaches_any_field: The adapter reads no member of a secret record beyond Match, Title and Description. Code, which would carry the surrounding source lines, is never consulted, and this fixture carries no Code and no Secret member at all. Nothing in this row is a secret value or a fragment of one.
row_derivations.path_refinement_unavailable_reason: _SECTION_PER_RECORD_PATH_FIELD is null for Secrets: ftypes.SecretFinding declares no path field, so the Target stands unrefined
row_derivations.start_line_note: A secret states StartLine directly. 312 is within the file's 2179 lines.
row_derivations.in_scope_note: python/pyspark/** covers every file beneath it, and the literal src/test appears nowhere in this path. The 832 python test modules under that root are in scope for the same reason; this file is not one of them.

row_derivations.scanner_class_source: the enclosing section array is Secrets
row_derivations.message_note: This record carries no Match, so the preference order falls through to Title. That is the reason Title and Description sit behind Match at all: a secret record without a Match still carries the words the tool wrote instead of earning a missing_message rejection.
row_derivations.start_line_note: 446, with the record's EndLine at 448. The row takes the start line; both are within the file's 2179 lines.

row_derivations.scanner_class_source: the enclosing section array is Vulnerabilities, which SUPPORTED_SECTIONS maps to vuln
row_derivations.severity_scores_not_consulted: The record carries three CVSS entries -- ghsa V3 7.5, nvd V2 7.8 and V3 7.5, redhat V3 7.5 -- and none is consulted, because HIGH is in the mapped label vocabulary and a mapped label governs. severity_native is the literal HIGH rather than a rendered score, which is what makes the precedence visible in the dataset itself.
row_derivations.path_refinement_absent_reason: the section does declare a per-record path field, PkgPath, but this record carries none, so the Target stands
row_derivations.start_line_absent_reason: A vulnerability declares no line information at all -- report.go puts StartLine on secrets and inside a misconfiguration's CauseMetadata, and nowhere on DetectedVulnerability. Absence is one of the five permitted absences and is never a rejection; an implementation that read absent as invalid would discard every Trivy vulnerability row, which is the largest silent loss this file guards against.
row_derivations.cwe_selection: The ascending-numeric rule takes the smallest integer after the CWE- prefix: 400 < 1333, so the emitted value is CWE-400 even though CWE-1333 is written first. This is the record whose producer order disagrees with the rule, and it is the only one in the fixture that does.
row_derivations.cve_source: /Results/2/Vulnerabilities/0/VulnerabilityID -- CVE-shaped, so it is emitted in cve as well as in rule_id
row_derivations.cve_note: VendorIDs carries GHSA-cph5-m8f7-6c5x and is deliberately not collected: a vendor advisory is not a CVE, and reshaping it into this field would be inference.
row_derivations.package_coordinate_level: 1 -- a package URL on the record itself
row_derivations.in_scope_note: dev/package-lock.json matches none of the twelve globs, so the row is kept with in_scope false. It is a real file in the pinned tree, 2168 lines; a runner legitimately reaching a manifest outside the twelve roots produces a kept row, never a rejection and never a halt.

row_derivations.scanner_class_source: the enclosing section array is Vulnerabilities
row_derivations.severity_note: UNKNOWN is a mapped literal, not an unmapped one: severity.py's label table bands NEGLIGIBLE, INFO, INFORMATIONAL, UNKNOWN and NONE to Info. So the basis is label, severity_native keeps UNKNOWN, severity_norm is Info, and severity_basis_unmapped_literal stays 0. severity_norm is never absent, whatever the literal.
row_derivations.start_line_absent_reason: a vulnerability declares no line information
row_derivations.cwe_absent_reason: this record carries no CweIDs member
row_derivations.cve_absent_reason: NSWG-ECO-519 is a Node.js Security WG identifier and is not CVE-shaped, so it stays in rule_id and cve is absent rather than being reshaped
row_derivations.package_coordinate_level: 2 -- a package URL on the matching enclosing Packages[] entry
row_derivations.package_coordinate_note: This is the level a reader most easily skips, and getting it wrong is the difference between pkg:npm/handlebars@4.5.3 and npm:handlebars@4.5.3. The record itself carries no PkgIdentifier, so level 1 fails; the enclosing Results[2].Packages holds an entry whose ID is handlebars@4.5.3, matched to this record's PkgID by exact equality, and that entry's Identifier.PURL is pkg:npm/handlebars@4.5.3. Level 2 precedes the ecosystem coordinate of level 3, so the PURL wins and the ecosystem route is never reached for this record.
row_derivations.package_coordinate_match_evidence: exact equality of /Results/2/Vulnerabilities/1/PkgID with /Results/2/Packages/1/ID -- no prefix match, no normalisation and no version-range reasoning
row_derivations.in_scope_note: dev/package-lock.json is outside the twelve globs; kept with in_scope false

row_derivations.scanner_class_source: the enclosing section array is Vulnerabilities
row_derivations.severity_scores_not_consulted: ghsa states a V3 score of 7.5 and a V4 score of 6.6 and nvd a V3 score of 7.5; the mapped label HIGH governs and none is consulted. Note that the two CVSS versions band differently -- 6.6 is Medium and 7.5 is High -- which is precisely why which entry was selected has to be recorded, and here the answer is that none was.
row_derivations.start_line_absent_reason: a vulnerability declares no line information
row_derivations.cwe_selection: one identifier, so the ascending rule is trivially satisfied and multi_valued_cwe_records is not incremented
row_derivations.package_coordinate_level: 1 -- a package URL on the record itself
row_derivations.in_scope_note: docs/Gemfile.lock matches none of the twelve globs; kept with in_scope false. It is a real file in the pinned tree, 89 lines.

row_derivations.scanner_class_source: the enclosing section array is Vulnerabilities
row_derivations.severity_scores_not_consulted: ghsa states a V4 score of 1.2 and nvd a V3 score of 5.3 -- Low and Medium respectively -- and the mapped label MEDIUM governs, so neither is consulted. Had the label been outside the vocabulary, the recorded selection would have had to name which of the two entries was used; the label spares that and the fact is recorded either way.
row_derivations.start_line_absent_reason: a vulnerability declares no line information
row_derivations.package_coordinate_note: This is the second of the two routes the fixture exercises. The record carries no PkgIdentifier, so level 1 fails; Results[3] carries no Packages inventory at all, so level 2 has no enclosing object to read; and level 3 forms bundler:rexml@3.3.8 from Type bundler, PkgName rexml and InstalledVersion 3.3.8. The ecosystem is lower-cased as the specified shape requires -- here it was already lower case, so the assertion that matters is the shape <ecosystem>:<name>@<version> and the separator placement rather than a case change.
row_derivations.in_scope_note: docs/Gemfile.lock is outside the twelve globs; kept with in_scope false

row_derivations.scanner_class_source: the enclosing section array is Vulnerabilities
row_derivations.severity_scores_not_consulted: ghsa V3 3.7, nvd V2 5.0 and V3 5.3, redhat V3 5.3; the mapped label LOW governs and none is consulted.
row_derivations.path_refinement_derivation: The enclosing Target is "Node.js", which names an ecosystem rather than a file. PkgPath names the manifest the package was found in. paths.resolve_trivy_path resolves the Target first, then applies the refinement: it is relative, it is neither the Target restated nor a suffix of it, and "Node.js" is not a container -- ARCHIVE_EXTENSIONS holds .jar .war .ear .zip .tar .tgz .tar.gz .aar .nupkg .whl .egg and not .js -- so it is joined onto the recorded scan_root base and relativized back, giving the manifest path unchanged. No archive-member serialization arises, and the row's path is a real file rather than the string "Node.js", which names nothing on disk.
row_derivations.counted_under: per_record_path_refinements, which is 1 for this fixture -- this row
row_derivations.start_line_absent_reason: a vulnerability declares no line information. The named file is five lines long, so had a line been emitted here it would have had to be within 1..5; none is.
row_derivations.cve_note: VendorIDs carries GHSA-gxpj-cx7g-858c and is not collected, for the same reason as row 4
row_derivations.package_coordinate_level: 1 -- a package URL on the record itself
row_derivations.in_scope_note: The refined path falls under core/src/main/**, so this row is in scope -- which is the point of resolving the refinement rather than keeping the Target: the unrefined "Node.js" would have matched no glob and taken in_scope false, turning a finding about an in-scope file into an out-of-scope row.
row_derivations.file_content_note: core/src/main/resources/org/apache/spark/ui/static/package.json is the only manifest-shaped file inside the twelve globs: five lines and eighty bytes carrying a name, a license and "type": "module", with no dependencies block and no lockfile beside it. This row is therefore the fixture's own illustration of a coordinate reported against a manifest that resolves no packages.

prohibitions_observed.no_secret_value_in_any_field: The only field on any row that carries material from a secret record's Match is row 2's message, and that Match is fifty-two asterisks -- Trivy's own redaction, with no character of a secret in it. No row carries a Secret member, a Code excerpt or any fragment of a matched value, and the adapter reads no secret-record member beyond Match, Title and Description. This tree is committed to git: the root .gitignore's only relevant line matches artifacts/, so nothing here is excluded from collection and the guarantee has to be structural rather than incidental.
prohibitions_observed.no_cross_tool_interpretation: Rows 4 to 8 are vulnerability findings and dependency-check's expected rows also carry vulnerability findings. Nothing here compares the two, ranks them, explains why one tool reported something another did not, or comments on a location both reached.
